Dragă Debbie

Freida McFadden, Mihaela Apetrei (Translator)

3.92
706,064 ratings60,200 reviews
Rate this book
„Ajută-mă, Debbie! Ce sfat îmi dai?”

Debbie Mullen simte că pierde controlul. Ani la rând, și-a adunat cele mai bune sfaturi în rubrica ei, „Dragă Debbie”, locul unde soțiile din New England veneau pentru înțelegere, alinare și un îndemn de la o femeie care pare să știe mereu ce are de făcut.

Prin scrisorile primite, Debbie a ascultat nenumărate povești ale unor femei ignorate, umilite, reduse la tăcere sau chiar abuzate de propriii soți. Iar ea a încercat, de fiecare dată, să le îndrume spre decizia corectă.

Acum, însă, viața ei se destramă cu o viteză uimitoare. Tocmai și-a pierdut slujba. Ceva ciudat se întâmplă cu fiicele ei adolescente. Iar soțul ei ascunde lucruri pe care Debbie începe să le descopere cu ajutorul aplicației de localizare instalate pe telefonul lui. Doar că Debbie nu mai are chef să fie femeia matură, rezonabilă, care trece totul cu vederea. Nu mai vrea să fie practică și calmă.

Așa că a decis să-și urmeze propriul sfat: fiecare trebuie să primească exact ce merită. Nici mai mult, nici mai puțin.

About the author

Freida McFadden

113 books309k followers
#1 New York Times, USA Today, Wall Street Journal, Publisher's Weekly, and Amazon Charts bestselling author Freida McFadden is a practicing physician specializing in brain injury who has penned multiple Kindle bestselling psychological thrillers and medical humor novels. She lives with her family and possessed cat in a centuries-old three-story home overlooking the ocean, with staircases that creak and moan with each step, and nobody could hear you if you scream. Unless you scream really loudly, maybe.

February 16, 2026
I gave McFadden three tries and I can now conclude it's not meant to be! Despite my desperate attempts to join the fanwagon, I just don't get the popularity of these books. Short chapters, I suppose. And very easy to read (nix the mention of rape and murder and my 8 year old would make quick work of this). But utterly ludicrous and hinged on at least ten different coincidences.

The protagonist is a housewife and part time columnist, but also a closeted genius who has complex apps tracking her entire family, and a penchant for petty revenge. Though, naturally, despite being the cleverest clever clogs that ever clevered, she doesn't think to turn off her location tracking when committing an actual crime 🫠

Plot-wise, it's a revenge fantasy. Revenge stories are great when done well, but they rely on the villains being despicable enough so we can enjoy the revenge, meaning that Debbie’s neighbours are atrociously obnoxious, the boss she wants to get revenge on is conveniently having an affair, and a high school coach is stupid enough to tell not only a teen girl but also her mother that she needs to lose a few pounds.

Genuinely, how do people deal with how ridiculously convenient things are? How convenient is Zane's criminal past? What luck her boss was having an affair! How wild the reveal about Ken? And, my god, the absolutely batshit thing with Harley and you-know-who?! MAJOR SPOILER:

I didn't guess the twist because I didn't count on that many absurd coincidences.

Then we get to the epilogue and I must have rolled my eyes about twenty times. It moves through the characters as they all reveal various new twists and wild coincidences. I was begging just STOP. I can only imagine there must be a bunch of readers who read this and think "oh my god, I never saw that coming, amazing" so each to their own. I am officially parting ways with McFadden's books.

I honestly wish Freida McFadden would release a new book every single week so my entire year could be brighter, twistier, smarter—and most importantly, endlessly entertaining—just like her unputdownable, incredibly addictive writing. Who am I kidding? Even if she released a book a day, I’d still struggle to keep up with the pace at which I devour them. Thankfully, she’s basically a writing machine and releases around three books a year… but is that enough?

No. Never. Absolutely not.

I know it’s early in the year, but I’m calling it now: when the Goodreads Choice Awards roll around—whether in the thriller category or any mystery-related award—this book already has my vote. It’s a more-than-five-stars read for me. And I’d also like to officially award myself a trophy for “Most Paranoid Twist-Catcher,” because for the first time ever while reading a McFadden book, I guessed all the twists… including the biggest one in the final third.

Yes, I shocked myself.

Clearly my McFadden Spidey senses have evolved. Since The Teacher-which had one of the most jaw-dropping, absolutely unforeseeable twists ever—I’ve trained myself to stay alert while reading her books. Honestly, I should thank her for providing the most entertaining form of brain exercise imaginable.

Now, let’s talk about this book—because it is unhinged in the best possible way.

One of the most common criticisms of McFadden’s books is the perceived naïveté of some of her characters. Some readers practically scream at the women in their reviews. (Side note: I will forever defend book-version Millie from The Housemaid—less… anatomy, more heart.)

But Debbie? Oh no. Debbie is a different beast.

Debbie is brilliant. A literal genius with a 178 IQ. She designs apps, left MIT for mysterious reasons, writes a popular advice column as Dear Debbie—empowering women with sharp, no-nonsense relationship advice—and balances all of this while being a stay-at-home mom to two teenagers in her early forties, plus a freelance writing career.

What no one seems to realize, though, is that Debbie can snap. When she witnesses injustice, something inside her ignites. Call it karma, call it vigilantism—but without a silly costume, Debbie delivers her own brand of justice to protect the people she loves.

And trust me… she’s about to explode.

Debbie is fuming—practically breathing fire like a Targaryen dragon. It all begins with the cancellation of her interview with a gardening magazine. She’s worked tirelessly to create a pastoral paradise in her backyard, only for her sneaky neighbor to steal her spotlight by secretly advertising her roses behind her back. And that’s just the tip of the iceberg.

She despises her daughter Lexi’s boyfriend, who not only empties their fridge but also their liquor cabinet. Her younger daughter Izzy is depressed after quitting soccer—could it have something to do with her creepy coach, rumored to be a peeping Tom lurking around the girls’ showers? Her husband is hiding something big… and yes, it might involve another woman. And then there’s Harley, her new gym friend, who seems way too invested in Debbie’s personal life. What are her real intentions?

But when an unexpected final crisis hits, Debbie completely unravels.

Twenty years ago, something happened to her—something she chose to ignore, to let slide. But she’s done playing the nice, agreeable housewife. Enough is enough. It’s time to take matters into her own hands.

Because nobody messes with our girl.

Bring it on, Debbie.

I don’t say this lightly, but Debbie might just be my favorite character Freida McFadden has ever created. Sorry, Millie—you’re iconic and unhinged in your own right, but Debbie is on another level. Wilder. Smarter. Even more dangerous. And that’s exactly why I loved her more.

This is my favorite thriller of the year so far. I had an amazing time reading it. I full-on villain-laughed out loud every time Debbie unleashed another vigilante move. I wholeheartedly recommend this book.

Absolute perfection.
My ideal popcorn-and-Cabernet read. 🍿🍷

Dear Debbie by Freida McFadden

This story was so entertaining and I feel bad for being entertained because it's also so wickedly evil. If you ever need help, write to Dear Debbie. She'll have to be diplomatic in her official letters but she has a secret file where she writes what you should really do if someone is giving you grief and the grief-maker just might not live through her advice.

While Debbie can dole out the advice, her life at home isn't running so smoothly. Her husband seems to keeping secrets and her daughters seem to think Debbie's ideas are at the bottom of the trash heap. She's not even allowed to talk to her oldest daughter, talk about losing control of a parent/child relationship. And, on top of everything, Debbie has just lost her job which doesn't mesh well with whatever is going on with her husband.

I can see Debbie, running amok and killing people decades from now, in some nursing home. She's that kind of character, always thinking, always scheming, always plotting, and everyone had better beware. This was a fun time while watching from afar (the other side of my Kindle).

4/5 ★

Dear Debby,

You are truly unhinged, but everyone will get why after reading this addictive, at times emotional revenge thriller.

Sincerely,
A Reader Who Couldn’t Look Away

In Dear Debbie, advice columnist Debbie Mullen is pushed to her breaking point when she loses her job and begins to suspect her husband is keeping secrets. As her life continues to collapse around her, Debbie stops trying to be the “bigger person” and decides it’s finally time to take her own advice and deliver payback to those who deserve it most.

I really liked this one! This is definitely going to be a hit with Freida McFadden fans. I’ve read so many of her books now I couldn’t even list them all, and she never misses for me (aside from The Crash last year).

This one had an extra layer that genuinely surprised me, compared to other Freida books I’ve read. Beyond the twists, deception, and absolutely unhinged characters, there was real heart here, and I found myself truly caring about Debbie and her family. Freida did an excellent job creating characters that felt believable and relatable to everyday families… just significantly more reckless. I especially loved the dynamic between Debbie and her teen daughters. Their comments toward her were hilarious and so real.

Debbie was easily the standout of the book, and she’s the kind of main character you won’t forget. She even reminded me a bit of the protagonist in Best Offer Wins (4.5 ★). I’m starting to love thrillers with characters who really go there and don’t hold back.

Like all of Freida’s books, this one is incredibly fast-paced and easy to sink into. The pages absolutely flew for me. I went into it while at the start of a reading slump, and once again she pulled me right out of it.

I don’t really have any major complaints. It wasn’t quite a five star read for me, but it was certainly entertaining.

I definitely recommend it!

FUN! 🍿

She sees them while they’re sleeping..she knows when they’re awake..

Diabolical Debbie Mullen is a loving mother and a doting wife, who keeps tabs on her family-with their permission-on the phone APP she designed called Findly.

She also writes an advice column aptly called “Dear Debbie” doling out UNCONVENTIONAL advice to New England wives who feel unappreciated by their husbands…(hilarious excerpts from these letters interspersed throughout)

But, it’s finally time to heed her own counsel…

It’s PAYBACK time for anyone and EVERYONE who has wronged her, or her family.

NO EXCEPTIONS

I was an outlier for “The Housemaid” finding it too OTT for my personal taste, but I have enjoyed some of the author’s short stories so when I was offered this book from the Publisher through Edelweiss, I decided to give this full length novel a try.

Did I find everything plausible? No, but I was entertained from the first page and I never lost interest!

The “Dear Debbie” column was an irresistible premise and those were some of my favorite chapters, but I admit I was completely SURPRISED by one of the other reveals too!

I also loved learning that Freida McFadden will always provide trigger warnings even though they might be spoilers, for sensitive readers and that her books will never have graphic descriptions of violence or SPICE. That is something that I am 100% onboard with.

NOW AVAILABLE!

Another day, another Freida McFadden read finished — and to my genuine surprise, I actually liked this one(don't mind the 3 star rating, it's a good version of it this time🫠). It’s easily one of her stronger recent releases. While it may not rank among my all-time favorites, it also wasn’t a frustrating waste of time, which, if you read enough thrillers, feels like a win.

One of the standout elements for me was the advice column format woven throughout the story. Those sections were engaging and added an extra layer of intrigue that kept me invested. I experienced this book via audiobook and honestly, that format probably saved me from abandoning it during slower stretches. The pacing swings between gripping and sluggish. Moments of real curiosity are followed by chapters that stall the momentum, creating a reading experience that feels both compelling and tedious.

A major win here: I genuinely enjoyed the female main character. That alone feels noteworthy, since her heroines often irritate me. This one was fun, sharp, and delightfully unhinged in a way that made her fascinating to follow. She may rank among my favorites to date and is absolutely the type of person you would not want to cross. Let’s just say karma plays a memorable role...💀🙈.

That said, there are moments later in the book that could have been handled with more nuance and care. Some developments feel rushed, and the novel occasionally overstays its welcome. Some moments that could've and should've been handled with more care and better worded than they were. A handful of chapters could have been chopped without losing anything essential.

As for the twists, they are unmistakably her style: bold, slightly outlandish, and requiring a healthy suspension of disbelief. Not the strongest reveals, but far from the weakest — very much a “just go with it” experience. Ultimately, the writing feels stronger than in some of her other recent works, which elevates the entire book. And in a rare turn for me, the epilogues were a highlight rather than an afterthought, providing a satisfying close instead of a coin toss.

Not perfect and not top-tier, but a solid, entertaining thriller that proves she still knows how to keep readers hooked, even when the ride gets a little uneven.

Holy Shooty Balls this one owned me! Viciously satisfying, darkly funny, & jaw dropping from start to finish!

Right away, there was this electric feeling that told me I was in the hands of a thriller that knew exactly what it was doing. Dear Debbie by Freida McFadden is a domestic thriller with claws and unapologetic energy that hooked me completely. I tore through all of it. Debbie kept my devoted interest from start to finish. The voice, the pace, the everything. I devoured it. The excerpts from the Dear Debbie column? I laughed out loud. Absolutely bingeable. And the fact that this is my very first Freida McFadden? I do not know what the heck I was waiting for.

Key Thoughts
📖 Pacing that never dipped. The chapters snapped forward with that addictive must keep reading momentum.
👀 Debbie. Debbie. Debbie. An all time favourite character for me. Her momma bear ferocity, her flaws, and that one moment that had both our hackles raised. I felt every beat of her.
💭 A wicked blend of humour and righteous fury. This is a story fuelled by women pushed past the edge and deciding enough is enough.
🏡 The setting gave me that creeping tension where everything looks perfect on the surface but you can feel something unsettling in the air just beneath it.
🧩 The twists were paced like detonations. One in particular shifted the entire landscape of the story with a single line. I sat back and just said wow.

This book completely wowed me. I am sitting here after finishing and I feel energized by what Freida McFadden just delivered. I am so glad I went in blind and let it hit me exactly the way it wanted to.

This is an unusual thriller. Debbie Mullen is, to all appearances, an ordinary homemaker with a husband and two children. She has a part time job writing an advice column for the local newspaper. But then her life spins out of control. Her boss fires her and her husband quits his job when he is denied partner status at his accounting firm. In addition, her older daughter is being blackmailed by her boyfriend, who has nude photos of her.
Debbie and her husband, Cooper, both have secrets which come to light in the book. Debbie decides to take control of her life with unexpected results. If you have ever daydreamed about taking revenge on the people that have wronged you, you will love this book.
One quote from the author, at the beginning of the book: "Even though my books are thrillers, a genre that traditionally has dark elements, I do my best to keep them as family friendly as I possibly can. You're not going to find any graphic scenes of violence or S-E-X."
I rate this book a solid 4 stars.
Thank you Lauren Klouda from Sourcebooks/Poisoned Pen Press for sending this eARC through Edelweiss+.

3.5 stars—- I’m sorry. …I was sick of reading dull, slow-paced (so called) thrillers and I relapsed. Yes, I turned to my old friend Freida for comfort and she didn’t disappoint. However, I now must enter rehab and return to stuffy, overhyped authors that never deliver the type of fast paced, thrill-rides that Freida does. Freida McFadden is great as a change of pace,don’t think about the inconsistencies, ridiculous plot twists that would never happen thriller writer … and I do mean THRILLER WRITER. “Dear Debbie” = expectations exceeded. Truthfully, Ms. McFadden has a gift of writing in such a relatable, easy to read manner that most of the books I’ve read of her’s I’ve thoroughly enjoyed (as long as I don’t over analyze). “Dear Debbie” tells the story of Debbie, her husband and two daughters who live a normal life in a normal neighborhood. Everything seems to be going great for Debbie and company until life happens and events don’t go the way Debbie thinks they should. When that happens, Debbie comes up with some creative solutions to change things up or get revenge in some of the more creative ways I have read. As the story progresses, Debbie’s methods get darker and the book takes some twists and turns that are unpredictable and absurd. I had to tell myself to not overthink it (or even to think at all)or it would ruin the momentum and fun. I definitely enjoyed the book — even the extreme twists and turns that would have had no chance of happening as written. I guess my willingness to overlook these type of problems tells you that the book delivered what I was looking for: a fun, interesting read that I could sit down and not think too hard about that just flew by. Thanks Freida —I’ll see you again in about 6 months.

[3.8⭐] 𝙌𝙪𝙚𝙧𝙞𝙙𝙖 𝘿𝙚𝙗𝙗𝙞𝙚 es un thriller psicológico escrito por Freida McFadden y publicado en 2026. La novela nos presenta a Debbie Mullen, una mujer que durante años ha sido la responsable de la popular columna de consejos «Querida Debbie», donde ayuda a otras mujeres a enfrentar sus problemas cotidianos con empatía y sensatez. Sin embargo, mientras intenta orientar la vida de los demás, la suya comienza a desmoronarse: pierde su trabajo, sospecha que su marido le oculta cosas y siente que sus hijas adolescentes cada vez se alejan más de ella.


Queridos lectores, me encanta Freida McFadden. Hay algo en sus libros que siempre logra atraparme, incluso cuando sé perfectamente cuál es su fórmula. Su forma de escribir es sencilla, los capítulos son muy cortos y eso hace que sus novelas se lean a una velocidad impresionante. Creo que esa capacidad de convertir una lectura en algo tan adictivo sigue siendo una de sus mayores fortalezas.

Además, cuando empiezo un libro suyo siempre tengo una expectativa muy clara: sé que en algún momento llegará un giro que me hará cuestionar todo lo que había pensado hasta ese instante. Hubo un plot twist que realmente no vi venir, me tomó completamente desprevenida y terminó siendo una de las cosas que más disfruté de la novela. Quizás no sea el giro más impactante que ha escrito la autora, pero sí consiguió sorprenderme cuando ya creía tener toda la historia resuelta.

Uno de los recursos que más me gustó fue la estructura de la narración. Los capítulos alternan entre el punto de vista de Debbie, el de su marido y los extractos de la columna "Querida Debbie". Este cambio constante hace que la lectura nunca se sienta monótona y, además, permite conocer la historia desde perspectivas muy distintas. Las cartas y las respuestas de la columna aportan un humor negro muy entretenido y funcionan como un contraste perfecto con la tensión que va creciendo en la trama.

También, disfruté la construcción del personaje de Debbie. Me pareció interesante ver cómo Freida desarrolla su evolución psicológica y cómo, poco a poco, vamos presenciando el deterioro emocional de una mujer que ha vivido intentando ser correcta, prudente y comprensiva con todos. A medida que las cosas empiezan a escaparse de su control, Debbie cambia, y aunque muchas de sus decisiones son moralmente cuestionables, nunca deja de resultar un personaje fascinante.

Debo decir que me agradó mucho la resolución de este conflicto. No crean que soy una psicópata, pero creo que todos alguna vez hemos fantaseado con que el karma llegue más rápido para ciertas personas o con hacer justicia con nuestras propias manos, aunque claramente sepamos que eso no es lo correcto. Justamente esa sensación es la que explora muy bien esta novela; Debbie lleva ese pensamiento al extremo y resulta inevitable preguntarse hasta dónde estaríamos dispuestos a llegar si nos encontráramos en una situación similar. No compartí muchas de sus acciones, pero sí entendí perfectamente de dónde nacían sus emociones.

Si tuviera que compararlo con otros libros de la autora, no diría que entra en mi top de favoritos, pero sí me pareció una de sus novelas más entretenidas de los últimos años. Tiene todos esos ingredientes que uno espera cuando toma un libro de Freida McFadden: capítulos cortos, una lectura muy ágil, personajes que esconden más de lo que aparentan, secretos, mentiras y giros inesperados que hacen que sea difícil dejar de leer.


Finalmente, puedo decir que 𝙌𝙪𝙚𝙧𝙞𝙙𝙖 𝘿𝙚𝙗𝙗𝙞𝙚 es una novela que disfruté bastante y que reafirma por qué sigo leyendo a Freida McFadden cada vez que publica un libro nuevo. No me pareció perfecta ni creo que sea su mejor obra, pero sí logró engancharme desde las primeras páginas, sorprenderme con un giro que no esperaba y hacerme disfrutar de una protagonista tan perturbadora como carismática.
